title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 2

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the inspection lesson take place?
tasks.audioText: The quality instructor will discuss inspection findings on Thursday at ten thirty. Students should bring the sample inspection sheet and meet in the maintenance classroom. The lesson will compare observed condition, acceptance criteria and recorded evidence. The instructor will explain why a report should distinguish an observation from a conclusion about the cause.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which inspection-results sheet is needed for the class?
tasks.audioText: The quality instructor will discuss inspection findings on Thursday at ten thirty. Students should bring the sample inspection sheet and meet in the maintenance classroom. The lesson will compare observed condition, acceptance criteria and recorded evidence. The instructor will explain why a report should distinguish an observation from a conclusion about the cause.

tasks.prompt: An inspection finding should describe what was observed and identify the relevant acceptance criterion. If a measurement is outside the stated limit, the report should include the actual value, unit and component reference. The inspector should avoid suggesting a cause unless the available evidence supports it. A clear finding allows the responsible person to review the issue and determine the next action. Reading 1. What should an inspection finding describe?
options: The inspector's opinion and a suggested repair
What was observed and the relevant acceptance criterion
The name of the person who ordered the component
The expected result without the actual observation

tasks.prompt: Which details should accompany an out-of-limit measurement?
options: To identify the technician's preferred measuring tool
To show where the inspection took place
To replace the need for a component reference
Actual value, unit and component reference

tasks.prompt: The actual value and unit ___ in the inspection report.
Choose TWO details that strengthen an inspection finding.
options: An unsupported guess about the cause

tasks.prompt: A rule or condition used to decide whether an item is acceptable is an acceptance ___.
You have observed a discrepancy but do not know its cause. What should you write?
options: The component failed because I think so.
The observed condition differs from the acceptance criterion; the cause has not been established.
The report should omit the result.
The issue is definitely caused by the last technician.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of inspection findings in a logical order.
options: State any limitation or unconfirmed cause
correctOrder: State any limitation or unconfirmed cause

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how to write a clear inspection finding. Include an observation, acceptance criterion and supporting evidence.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total. Score each criterion 0–2: (1) Observation — 2: states a factual, specific and measurable finding without assumptions; 1: partly specific; 0: missing or speculative. (2) Acceptance criterion — 2: identifies the relevant requirement or limit for comparison; 1: vague reference; 0: absent. (3) Evidence — 2: identifies traceable measurements, records or inspection evidence; 1: limited evidence; 0: absent or invented. (4) English — 2: clear structure and accurate inspection/quality vocabulary; 1: errors but meaning clear; 0: meaning frequently unclear.
